svg.text: One die: a hard RISC-V subsystem and FPGA fabric, joined by a narrow bridge. Every term the later slides use is named here.
eNVM -- 128 KB non-volatile, holds the application
built from: LSRAM (20 Kb blocks) . uSRAM . MACC (18x18)
MSS and fabric BOTH reach DDR, but not coherently: FIC_0 is outside the cache, so
anything the CPU writes for a kernel must be flushed first, and anything a kernel
writes must be invalidated before the CPU reads it. That single fact shapes most of
SCALE, so the later numbers land: the whole device holds ~4.4 MB on chip against a
256 MB frame. 784 MACC blocks, of which the shipping design uses 74. It is BANDWIDTH
-bound, not compute-bound -- which is why the architecture is about deleting DDR
